title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 10 introduces a second kind of morphism between 'MD-graphs' (Mumford–Deligne dual graphs of stable marked curves), called 'normalisation morphisms'. They complement the generalisation (edge-contraction) morphisms already used. The aim is to account for maps between boundary strata such as M_G → M_{g_α, Î_α} and forgetful maps M^π_{g,I} → M_{g,I'}. Normalisation morphisms and generalisation morphisms are meant to intersect exactly in isomorphisms.

On this page Grothendieck takes a stable marked curve (X̂, I) over an algebraically closed field k, with open part X = X̂ \ I and set of double points A. He chooses a subset I' ⊂ I of points at infinity and a subset A' ⊂ A of nodes. From these he builds a curve X' that has I' as points at infinity and A' as double points:
- Normalise X̂ at the nodes in A \ A', giving X̂'.
- Set X' = X̂' \ I'. The points of I \ I' are thereby turned back into ordinary points (the 'bord de la tranche' relative to those i).

He warns that X̂' maps to X̂ but not to the further object written with a double hat, unless I' = I.

The construction is explicit once (I', A') is given. In terms of the dual graph C of X, the data amount to:
- a subgraph C' ⊂ C with the same vertex set, i.e. some edges deleted;
- a subset I' of the legs.

The graph of X' is then that subgraph. The next page refines this by recording the 2·|A \ A'| preimages J̃ of the normalised nodes as new marked points. That turns the normalisation into the familiar partial-normalisation / gluing situation. In modern terms this is the passage from a stable graph Γ to the graph obtained by cutting edges into pairs of legs and dropping legs. These are the morphisms underlying the clutching maps ∏ M̄_{g_v,n_v} → M̄_{g,n} and the forgetful maps. Together with contractions they generate the graph category used for modular operads and for the stratification of M̄_{g,n}.
errors: As stated on this page (forgetting both J̃ and I\I'), X' need not be stable and its graph C' may be disconnected. The subgraph-with-legs-I' description therefore does not by itself give an object of the same moduli type. Grothendieck evidently notices this, since the next page reinstates the preimages J̃ as marked points.

Forgetting the legs in I\I' generally requires stabilisation (contracting unstable components). The graph of X' is then not literally the subgraph C' when components become unstable. This is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Normalisation morphisms of dual graphs: delete a subset of edges (cut nodes) and a subset of legs (forget marked points), complementary to contraction (generalisation) morphisms, intersecting in isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Graph morphisms of stable graphs combining edge contractions with cutting/grafting and leg-forgetting (category of stable graphs for modular operads; gluing/clutching and forgetful maps of M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (clutching/forgetful maps, 1983); Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Borisov–Manin (graph categories, 2007)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower, but does not spell out this graph formalism

ideas.what: Partial normalisation of a stable curve at a chosen set of nodes, described via Y/σ_{Ã'}

missed.claim: An early, independent formulation of a category of dual graphs of stable marked curves with two classes of morphisms, generalisation (contraction) and normalisation (edge cutting plus leg forgetting), intersecting in isomorphisms. This anticipates the graph categories later used for modular operads. It is standard material today.
missed.quote: On va introduire pour ceci une notion de morphisme de MD-graphes, contenant notion de morphismes de normalisation (l'intersection des deux notions de morphisme est celle d'iso de MD-graphes)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck organising the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} combinatorially along the lines later formalised by Getzler–Kapranov and Borisov–Manin. There is no new mathematics here.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine partial-normalisation construction and its translation into dual graphs. The only point of interest is the historical anticipation of a combined contraction/cutting graph category, which is now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'obtient-on' is better read as 'on obtient' / 'obtenue en'. The sense is 'obtained by taking a bord-de-la-tranche relative to i ∈ I\I' and normalising X at the points of A\A''.
'= ensemble des sommets' is Grothendieck's shorthand for 'même ensemble des sommets' (a spanning subgraph).
The final words read 'Le [MD-crossed out]-sous-graphe' and probably begin 'Le MD-graphe' or 'Le MD-sous-graphe', continued on the next page as '... complétée de X'.'
